votes.reasoning: I compared the old SecurityToolCredentialReader.runTool with BoundedProcess.run line by line, and the behavior is the same. (1) Launch: stdin is FileHandle.nullDevice, stderr is nullDevice, stdout is a Pipe, and the terminationHandler semaphore is set before run(). A launch error still maps to Failure.launchFailed (SecurityToolCredentialReader.swift:136-142). (2) Draining: stdout is still read to EOF on a global userInitiated queue behind OSAllocatedUnfairLock, before any wait, so a large output cannot deadlock (BoundedProcess.swift:53-60). (3) Kill escalation: one deadline for exit, then terminate, 1 s, SIGKILL, 1 s, then a 1 s drain wait. Same order, same budgets (BoundedProcess.swift:65-72). (4) Race window: the old code accepted a child that had drained, was not running, exited with reason .exit and status 0, and decoded. The new check is `outcome.exitedCleanly && decodeOutput` (SecurityToolCredentialReader.swift:147), and exitedCleanly is drained && terminationReason == .exit && status == 0, where terminationReason is nil while the child still runs (BoundedProcess.swift:35,78-82). That is the same condition. (5) Normal exit with the drain missing the deadline: before, this threw timedOut with no race-window check. Now timedOut = !drainedInTime and exitedCleanly needs drained, so it still throws timedOut. (6) Status check: before, `guard terminationStatus == 0` did not look at terminationReason, so a signal number surfaced as exited(status:). Now outcome.status is terminationStatus whenever the child is not running, so the result is the same. The payload is never logged, and the cooldowns are unchanged (they live outside runTool). hdiutil in DMGVerifier.swift:113-122 fails closed on timedOut, so it deliberately does not accept the race window, which is right for a trust decision. The distinct failure cases (launchFailed, timedOut, hdiutilExited, mountFailed, detachFailed, noSingleApp, signatureRejected, invalidTeamID) are in place. Tests: `scripts/with-test-toolchain.sh swift test --no-parallel --filter "UpdateChecker|TeamSignatureDMGVerifier|SecurityToolCredentialReader|BoundedProcess|KeychainCredentialReader"` gave 85 tests in 11 suites, all passing, including the credential-fallback lifecycle tests (hung tool killed, cooldowns, non-zero exit, missing executable, real security tool in a temp keychain). Reversal: I backed up UpdateChecker.swift to the scratchpad and put back the fail-open behavior (nil checksum means download without a check, at UpdateChecker.swift:251 and :288). "release without a parseable checksum fails closed" then went RED (UpdateCheckerDownloadTests.swift:104-105). I restored the file byte-identical, and `git diff HEAD` equals the saved SEC-CER-001.diff. No git stash was used. Caveat, not blocking: if `hdiutil attach` hits the 60 s timeout right after mounting, verifyBlocking throws before the detach defer is registered (DMGVerifier.swift:69-74). A read-only mount can then be left under the temp dir. It fails closed, so there is no security impact, only a leak.

Both round-1 required changes are in the updated diff. (1) Duplication: there is now one copy of the launch, drain and kill logic, in Sources/AiTaskbarCore/Util/BoundedProcess.swift:495-539 (diff lines 495-539). It runs with null stdin and stderr, drains stdout on a background thread, uses a single deadline, sends SIGTERM and then SIGKILL, and all of that sits in one place. SecurityToolCredentialReader.runTool (diff 387-448) went from about 50 lines to about 20 and delegates to it. That reader keeps its race-window acceptance as its own logic through `outcome.exitedCleanly`, so it behaves the same: `exitedCleanly` requires `drained`, which matches the old `drainedInTime` check. TeamSignatureDMGVerifier.runHdiutil (DMGVerifier.swift:164-174) is now 10 lines of mapping only. (2) Error naming: Failure now has separate cases, `launchFailed(String)`, `timedOut`, `hdiutilExited(Int32)` (which keeps the exit status) and `indirect detachFailed(Failure)`. `mountFailed` is now used only where the attach plist has no mount point (DMGVerifier.swift:160). The detach log wraps the real cause (DMGVerifier.swift:126-132). The new helper's API is reasonable. It is a caseless `enum` namespace. `Outcome: Sendable` is a value type that carries only facts. `terminationReason` is nil while the child is still running, which avoids reading `Process.terminationReason` on a live process (that raises an exception). `exitedCleanly` is named for exactly what it checks. The doc comment says the call blocks for up to timeout + ~3 s and that callers must keep it off the cooperative pool. The DMG verifier follows that by running it in `Task.detached`. `try process.run()` passes its error up instead of swallowing it. The only `try?` in the diff is cleanup of the temp root, which CLAUDE.md allows. There is no new wrapper or ceremony, and the new Core file has tests as CLAUDE.md §4 requires (BoundedProcessTests: happy path, non-zero exit, timeout, SIGKILL after an ignored TERM, launch failure). Those tests use only non-optional `#expect` asserts, which the Bool rule allows. Two small points, neither enough to change the vote. First, `status` is set to a 0 sentinel when `terminationReason == nil`. That is documented, but a caller that forgets to check could misread it as a clean exit. Second, `hdiutilExited` also carries the signal number when hdiutil dies from a signal. I did not build this, as instructed, so I have not measured warnings. `Outcome: Sendable` holding `Process.TerminationReason`, an imported ObjC enum, is expected to be Sendable, but that is not confirmed by a compile.

Round 2 only widened the diff in the way QUALITY asked for. 12 files are touched. The 9 from round 1 are unchanged in scope. The 3 new ones are: Sources/AiTaskbarCore/Util/BoundedProcess.swift (the shared helper QUALITY asked for), Tests/AiTaskbarCoreTests/BoundedProcessTests.swift (the '@Test for a new Core file' rule), and SecurityToolCredentialReader.swift, whose only change is runTool (hunk @@ -132,56 +132,26 @@).

I traced the runTool refactor and it keeps the same behavior:
- Arguments, stdin /dev/null and stderr discarded are all still set, now inside BoundedProcess.run.
- SIGTERM, then SIGKILL 1 s later, is the same sequence.
- The race-window case (child finished right at the deadline) accepted exactly this: drained, not running, terminationReason .exit, status 0. That is what Outcome.exitedCleanly checks now.
- The drain timeout when the child had already exited used to throw timedOut. It now sets timedOut = !drainedInTime, exitedCleanly is false, and it still throws Failure.timedOut.
- A launch error still maps to Failure.launchFailed, and a non-zero status to Failure.exited.

The credential fallback contract in CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md:551 (exact-match arguments, stdin /dev/null, stderr discarded, 5 s budget that kills the child, cooldown, readOffPool, never used for writes) still describes the code accurately. No doc names runTool or its internals, so nothing went stale. The only doc for BoundedProcess is its own header comment. It correctly names both callers (security, hdiutil).

The existing SecurityToolCredentialReaderTests suite is untouched. It keeps covering the reader's behavior across the refactor.

Public surface: BoundedProcess is a new public enum in Core. It is needed because the App target (DMGVerifier.swift:114-121) consumes it. It adds no dependency, host, secret or entitlement. `import os` is still needed in SecurityToolCredentialReader.swift:2, because OSAllocatedUnfairLock is used at :71.

The docs are in sync with the fix: README, CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md (identical), and all 3 localization files.
new_findings: INFO (SCOPE/tests): BoundedProcessTests starts real /bin/sh and /bin/sleep children with a 0.3 s budget and asserts timing under 5-6 s. It depends on the host, the same way the round-1 hdiutil tests do. That is fine on macOS runners, but it could flake on a very overloaded CI machine.

INFO (SCOPE/API): BoundedProcess.Outcome.status is 0 when terminationReason is nil (the child survived the SIGKILL wait). Both callers check timedOut before they read status, so no wrong result escapes today. A future caller that reads status alone would see a false 0. Consider making status optional in a follow-up.
